answer: Each agent locks a 70-credit bond on a quartz-timed node and joins the river of heartbeat proofs. A public beacon acts as a prism, splitting the river at a random point and spot-checking the slice for a fresh quartz-stamped heartbeat. A missed beat or reused serial burns it. The first proof costs 40, the k-th 40+6(k-1); 1,000 fakes cost 3,037,000 plus 70,000 locked against a 40,000 pool, so renting heartbeats loses. An honest agent pays 40 once.
